# Cycle detection for AI agents

AI agents can get stuck in loops, calling the same tool with the same arguments
and getting the same results while every request succeeds. Cycle detection, part
of Agentic Analytics in Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric, finds these unproductive
loops so that Consul can then open the affected agent's circuit according to
behavior policy.

@include '../../../global/partials/alerts/beta.mdx'

To set it up, refer to [Configure cycle detection](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/cycle-detection/configure-cycle-detection).

@include 'alerts/enterprise-alert.mdx'

## Introduction

Mesh resilience features, such as [circuit
breaking](/consul/docs/reference/proxy/envoy#proxy-upstream-config-options),
cannot detect when an agent gets stuck in an unproductive loop because the
upstream services stay available and responsive. 

For example, an agent repeatedly invokes `query_records` with
`{"filter":"status:active","page":1}` and receives the same records each time.
Summarizing unchanged results does not advance its task. Cycle detection
analyzes the workflow's steps and results to find this repetition.

The circuit is agent scoped. It contains the affected agent without blocking
other agents that use the same upstream service.

Analysis runs asynchronously. Agentic Analytics evaluates trace evidence, and
Consul's enforcement path checks the resulting protection state before it allows
later requests.

Note that enabling mesh circuit breaking does not enable cycle detection.

## How cycles are detected

A finding requires both a repeated structure and repeated results. Agentic
Analytics' cycle detector looks for the same agent repeating a tool call with
the same argument values within a workflow. It does not only count calls to a
tool.

### Structural check

Agentic Analytics cycle detector reduces the trace to an ordered sequence of
workflow steps, such as tool calls, delegations, and summaries. It finds maximal
runs of a repeating unit and collapses duplicate matches. Runs that meet the
configured minimum repetition count go to the semantic check.

A repeating unit can be one step, such as `query_records` with the same filter
and page values. It can also be two steps, such as a call followed by a summary.
For a multi-step unit, the detector compares each tool call's arguments with the
same call in the other repetitions.

### Semantic check

Agentic Analytics cycle detector compares outputs at the same position across
repetitions. Each retrieval result is compared with the other retrieval results,
and each summary with the other summaries. A retrieval result is never compared
with a summary.

Outputs are reduced to their values before comparison, so shared field names
alone do not make different results match. Identical outputs match directly.
Otherwise, Agentic Analytics cycle detector compares text embeddings against a
configurable similarity threshold.

Agentic Analytics cycle detector reports a candidate as unproductive when at
least one position repeats the same or a sufficiently similar result across
passes. Not every position has to stay unchanged. Review this behavior for
workflows with deliberately stable intermediate results.

### What is not a cycle

- An agent that changes the `page` argument and retrieves new records makes
  progress, even though it repeats the tool name.
- A call with unchanged arguments can return new data when the underlying state
  changes.
- A structural match alone does not open the circuit. The semantic check must
  also match.

A finding is evidence for behavior policy. It does not prove that the whole task
failed or that all repeated work was unnecessary.

## How detection and enforcement work

| Stage | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Proxy auto-instrumentation | The AI Inference Gateway and MCP sidecars emit correlated spans with tool identity and approved argument and result evidence. |
| Trace producer | Queue trace IDs on a BullMQ queue as workflow evidence arrives. |
| Trace backend | Store spans and make them queryable. |
| Agentic Analytics | Consume queued trace IDs, fetch spans, and run the structural and semantic checks. |
| Behavior policy | Evaluate findings and decide whether to open the agent's circuit. |
| Protection-state storage | Publish the agent-scoped circuit state, its reason, and its validity period. |
| Enforcement processor | Check applicable state before forwarding a later request through the Consul data plane. |

The queue carries trace IDs, and the worker retrieves spans from the trace
backend. A trace ID can be queued several times as the workflow grows. Agentic
Analytics' cycle detector runs single traces serially and different traces run
concurrently up to the configured limit.

Analysis does not hold the original application request open while it waits
for evidence. When a trace is not yet complete, Agentic
Analytics cycle detector analyzes it again during a later pass.

When the circuit is open, the enforcement processor rejects later applicable
requests from the agent with HTTP `503`. It does not cancel calls that already
passed enforcement or reverse completed tool actions.

Agentic Analytics cycle detector depends on
[auto-instrumentation](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/auto-instrumentation) for its
evidence. Applications preserve trace context across calls and supply business
outcomes that the proxies cannot see. Missing context or unsupported traffic
limits what the detector can assess.

## Protection state and recovery

| State | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Closed | Requests proceed when they satisfy the other applicable controls. |
| Open | Requests from the affected agent are rejected. |

Store the agent identity, policy context, reason, and validity period with each
decision, so enforcement can tell applicable protection from stale state.

Recovery follows the configured expiry or reset rules. A time-to-live (TTL)
expires the state automatically, and an operator reset is a separate action.
Neither shows that the agent's behavior is fixed. Do not assume a half-open
probe state unless the deployed component supports it.

## Limitations

- **Delay**. Detection follows execution, trace export, indexing, analysis, and
  state publication. The agent can act again before enforcement sees an open
  circuit. Cycle detection cannot prevent a first unsafe action, recall an
  in-flight call, or undo a completed side effect.
- **Missing evidence**. Missing spans, sampling, unavailable output, redaction,
  and analysis backlog can prevent or delay a finding. Trace export and indexing
  can lag behind queue delivery. An empty trace or the absence of a finding does
  not show that a workflow is healthy. Monitor analysis lag, failed jobs, trace
  availability, state freshness, circuit transitions, and enforcement
  rejections.
- **Dependency failures**. No universal fail-open or fail-closed choice exists
  for unavailable analytics or state storage. Define the behavior for each
  workload.
- **Scope**. Agentic Analytics owns cycle analysis, and Consul acts on its
  findings through behavior policy and agent-scoped enforcement. Cycle detection
  supplements synchronous authorization, usage limits, human approval, and
  application validation. It does not replace them, and it does not prove model
  quality or task completion.
- **Application responsibility**. Applications own planning, tool business
  logic, and recovery from side effects.
- **Privacy**. Trace evidence, comparison inputs, and findings stay subject to
  telemetry privacy, access control, and retention requirements. Do not copy
  sensitive comparison values into circuit reasons, metrics, or logs.
